summary: Schoharie County, NY tower built 1940, closed 1971, then county radio use; moved 1999-2002 and rebuilt as the Knightower in West Hurley, Ulster County.

facts.design: 67-foot-6-inch steel International Derrick tower (Wikipedia); a 1939 newspaper had announced a 65-foot tower
facts.status_note: Mountain tower taken down; the relocated tower stands as the Knightower in West Hurley, Ulster County

access.note: Wikipedia says the original tower site is closed to the public; the Knightower is privately owned and its owner shows it with permission

visit.trail_note: Knightower: contact the owner; coordinates are unlisted at the owner's request (NHLR)

facts.agency: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (Wikipedia); later Schoharie County; now privately owned as the Knightower

events.note: Press and Sun-Bulletin reported a planned 65-foot tower on Petersburg Mountain
Civilian Conservation Corps built a 67-foot-6-inch International Derrick tower (Wikipedia); NHLR gives Built 1940
First staffed in 1941; 7 fires and 223 visitors reported that year
In April, observers agreed to scan the skies and report to the Albany Filter Center after a meeting with Air Force defense officials
Six-year-old boy died in a fall from the tower in August; state police said he apparently slipped from the platform
Lorna Borst named as forest fire observer at the Petersburg Mountain tower
Tower closed at the end of the 1971 season as aerial detection came into wider use for fire watching
Schoharie County bought the tower for $10 for communications use
Six juveniles arrested for allegedly breaking into the communications center at the tower
Al Moulin had the tower trucked to his property in Esperance, NY (NHLR)
Barry Knight took possession of the steel and moved it to West Hurley (NHLR); the firelookout list places it in Ulster County; Wikipedia says the tower was sold to Knight and relocated
Four piers poured in September 2004; Knight reassembled the tower on Ashokan Ridge
Knightower opened to visitors in July 2006; 43 feet to the top railing

corrections.why: 19.8 m (65 ft) matches the 1939 announcement of a planned tower; Wikipedia gives the built tower as 67 ft 6 in (20.57 m)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1939 newspaper announced a 65-foot tower. Wikipedia and the NHLR both date the built tower to 1940, and Wikipedia gives 67 ft 6 in. The story uses 1940 and 67 ft 6 in and notes the plan.

resolved_conflicts.field: ownership and route to West Hurley
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the tower was sold to Barry Knight and relocated to West Hurley. The NHLR adds a 1999 move to Esperance under Al Moulin and a 2002 handover to Knight. The story gives the NHLR route and notes that Wikipedia does not mention Esperance.

notes_for_editor: Original site: firelookout lists it as gone and Wikipedia says an antenna support structure replaced the tower, with no date and no ground check. The Knightower (NHLR US 988, NY 33) is a private platform tower, so a relocated link may suit the record. Owner contact and coordinates are left out on purpose. Brief access 'unknown' is now closed per Wikipedia. The 1953 fatal fall is included as a sourced incident; the editor may cut it. Confidence is medium because of the height and ownership conflicts and the missing removal date.
